public_rationale: Data Center Knowledge reported on October 9, 2026 that the RELLIS developer filed for bankruptcy in November 2025, leaving the project unfinished [e1]. The same report says ThisWay Global acquired the project on September 30, 2026 and planned to convert it to AI use; it provides no calculation of project costs or recovery [e1]. American Compute's compilation, updated October 17, 2026, reports no public foreclosure of a GPU-backed loan, but covers compute-credit distress rather than final data-center project accounts [e2]. These items establish neither $200 billion in permanent project failures with recovery below 25% nor a complete accounting that excludes that outcome [e1, e2].
limitations: Verified project costs and project-level recovery calculations are missing.
The RELLIS report does not establish that the project qualified as an AI project at publication.
The compute-credit compilation is not a comprehensive accounting of data-center project outcomes.
The forecast supplies no deadline, project list or accounting basis for cost recovery.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: At least $200 billion of data centers will collapse before recovering even a quarter of their costs.

statement.excerpt: There are, I believe, at least $200 billion worth of data centers that will never make even a quarter of their costs back before collapsing, and that’s assuming that they ever turn on or their customers exist by the time they do so.

from_speaker: at least $200 billion worth of data centers
will never make even a quarter of their costs back
assuming that they ever turn on
our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion identifies AI data-center projects, including unfinished projects, as the subject.
The ordinary reading is permanent commercial failure before recovering 25% of project costs. A temporary delay, financing default, or change of ownership does not alone establish that outcome.
The projects must already exist or be identifiable as planned projects at the post date. Costs must not be counted twice across owners, lenders, and equipment suppliers.
The speaker supplies neither an accounting basis nor a definition of cost recovery. Both must be resolved before a monetary threshold can receive a decisive score.
criteria.support_condition: Identified eligible projects permanently fail with verified aggregate project costs of at least USD 200 billion, each recovering less than 25% of its costs before failure.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A complete accounting of the eligible project population establishes that projects failing below the recovery threshold total less than USD 200 billion, with every remaining project already recovering at least 25% or otherwise having a final outcome that excludes qualification.

evidence.explanation: This identifies a distressed project, but the report describes its subsequent acquisition and planned conversion from conventional colocation to AI use. It supplies no qualifying project-cost and recovery calculation.

evidence.excerpt: No GPU-backed loan has been publicly foreclosed.
evidence.explanation: The compilation does not establish a qualifying foreclosure event. Its coverage concerns compute credit, and cannot establish either the success or failure of the broader project forecast.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Define the eligible publication-date projects and a consistent accounting basis. Final records showing permanent failures with aggregate project costs of at least $200 billion, each recovering less than 25% of its costs, would support the forecast. Contradiction requires complete final accounting showing qualifying failures below $200 billion, with every remaining project excluded by sufficient recovery or another final outcome.
